gaps_found.title: Product/category CTAs do not pass product context into RFQ or sample forms
gaps_found.measurement: 0 of 84 English product pages pass a product query parameter on their Request Pricing/Request Sample CTAs (grepped directly)
gaps_found.root_cause: CTA hrefs were never updated to the parameter-passing convention already used by jft-conversion.js's article buyer-path and quote-calculator.js; contact.html's dropdown covers only ~20 broad categories, not all 84 specific products, so a naive fix would still silently lose context for most products
gaps_found.affected_pages: all 84 english product pages + up to 840 locale product-page copies (same CTA pattern, locale-safe because contact.html option `value` attributes stay in English across all locales)

gaps_found.title: RTL breadcrumb chevrons point the wrong direction on every Arabic page
gaps_found.measurement: jft-design-system.css:235 .jft-breadcrumb has no RTL-specific icon rule; ar/*.html sets html dir=rtl but the chevron glyph (fa-chevron-right) is not mirrored
gaps_found.root_cause: shared breadcrumb component never accounted for RTL icon mirroring
gaps_found.affected_pages: every Arabic (ar/) page using .jft-breadcrumb - effectively the entire Arabic site

a category represents a commodity group, not one SKU; a forced product guess would misleadingly preselect the wrong specific grade in contact.html's dropdown - worse than no preselection

commercial_ux_scores.scoring_note: 0-10 per dimension, not artificially inflated. Scored on the state found DURING THE AUDIT, i.e. before Gap 1/2 fixes below.

score_interpretation.weakest_dimension_before_fixes: friction and cta_relevance on contact.html, sample-request.html, and product pages - directly caused by Gap 1 (lost product context forces re-entry)
score_interpretation.weakest_page_type: arabic pages score identically to English on every dimension except navigation, which is dragged down specifically by Gap 2 (breadcrumb chevron direction)
score_interpretation.highest_value_improvement: Gap 1 fix (product-context preservation) - raises friction and cta_relevance scores on the 3 most commercially important page types (product, contact, sample-request) simultaneously, using entirely pre-existing infrastructure
